scripting.why: A script builds hundreds of parts and sends them in a few requests: much faster than single tool calls.
scripting.remote: Game in the cloud (streamed): the kit is on YOUR machine at the path in the UNREAL_KIT environment variable (Connect.bat sets it, with UNREAL_RELAY and UNREAL_TOKEN); uk.connect() then goes through the relay by itself. Do not search the disk.
scripting.fastest: Cities and streets: uk.district("manhattan" | "paris" | "london" | ... , blocks=(3, 2)) builds a whole district (streets, styled buildings, trees) in one call in seconds; every run is different. Single buildings: from unreal_kit import buildings as B; B.building(kind, style=...).
scripting.how: Python: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, r'<kit>'); import unreal_kit as uk. It connects by itself to the game on this machine (uk.connect(url='http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp') for another port). uk.tools.<toolset>.<tool>(...) is every tool; uk.parts builds part lists (box, cyl, sphere, beam, extrude, sweep, transform, grid, ring, PALETTE materials); uk.place / uk.place_many / uk.batch send them in big requests; uk.rules builds game rules; uk.ui builds layout UI; uk.look sets light, cameras and takes review images. <examples> has readable example scripts (city, game pieces, combat presets) to copy from. Use the files where they are: do not download code and do not print environment variables. Save good results with scene.save_template. Skill python_kit has the details.
